//: Opt-in: run OpenAI Codex from inside Claude Code. Reference only — do NOT @-import this file. Copy the two blocks below into your own settings.json (or settings.local.json) and merge enabledPlugins with the block already there.
//why: The point of this one is FAILOVER, not review: when Claude tokens run low, hand the expensive work to Codex instead of stopping. See README.md → 'Codex as a failover' for the playbook.
//prerequisites: 1) A ChatGPT subscription (Free tier included) or an OpenAI API key — usage counts against your CODEX limits, not your Claude limits, which is the entire point. 2) Node.js >= 18.18. 3) The Codex CLI: `npm install -g @openai/codex`, then `codex login`. After enabling, run `/codex:setup` — it reports whether Codex is ready and can install it for you if npm is available.
//not-in-the-baseline: Deliberately NOT in the checked-in settings.json, for three reasons: (a) it needs external credentials, so the same rule as MCP servers applies — consumers opt in rather than have it forced on; (b) it comes from a THIRD-PARTY marketplace, so unlike claude-plugins-official it needs the extraKnownMarketplaces block below; (c) its /codex:review and /codex:adversarial-review overlap commands this repo already ships (/grill, /rabbit, code-architect), and the baseline rule is to avoid duplicating our own command surface.
//heads-up: Enabling a plugin also enables its hooks. This one registers SessionStart, SessionEnd, and a Stop-time review gate whose timeout is 900s — the plugin describes that gate as optional, so check `/codex:setup` and the plugin's own docs before running it somewhere a long Stop hook would be disruptive (e.g. an automated loop).
//what-you-get: Commands: /codex:rescue (delegate work to Codex, write-capable, backgroundable, resumable), /codex:transfer (turn THIS Claude session into a resumable Codex thread), /codex:status, /codex:result, /codex:cancel, /codex:review, /codex:adversarial-review. Plus the `codex:codex-rescue` subagent, visible in /agents.
//pinning: A marketplace source may set `ref` (branch or tag) but NOT `sha`. Add `"ref": "<tag>"` inside the source block below if you want to pin rather than track the default branch.
